children: Shares of IndusInd Bank Ltd. gained around 1% on Monday, October 26, after the private sector lender reported a return to profitability in the second quarter of FY27, alongside an improvement in asset quality and lower provisions. However, continued pressure on net interest margins (NIM) remains a key concern.
IndusInd Bank reported a net profit of ₹1,242 crore for the quarter, compared with a loss of ₹437 crore in the year-ago period.

Net interest income (NII) increased 3.6% year-on-year to ₹4,569 crore from ₹4,409 crore. Operating profit, excluding provisions and other adjustments as indicated in the source data, rose 40.4% to ₹2,875 crore from ₹2,047 crore.
Asset quality improved sequentially, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 2.73% from 3.25% in the previous quarter. Net non-performing assets (NNPA) fell to 0.83% from 0.95%.
Management expects loan growth to broadly track industry growth, with a focus on secured retail lending and loans to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
The bank expects to recover the compression in NIM over the next two quarters. Foreign currency non-resident (FCNR(B)) deposits affected NIM by 7-8 basis points during the quarter.
IndusInd Bank is targeting a return on assets (RoA) of 1% by the fourth quarter of FY27, while its medium-term aspiration remains 1.75%-1.8%.

Management sees limited scope for a further meaningful reduction in credit costs, indicating that the next phase of profitability recovery will increasingly depend on margin improvement and fee income.
In microfinance, growth has resumed after nearly eight quarters. However, the bank remains cautious about lending in drought-affected areas of Karnataka, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.

Macquarie has an 'Underperform' rating on IndusInd Bank, with a target price of ₹760 per share. The brokerage said the bank's profit beat estimates, supported by stronger non-interest income. RoA improved despite pressure on margins, although headwinds remain.

Management reiterated its target of achieving a 1% exit RoA by the fourth quarter of FY27, compared with the reported level of 0.82%. Macquarie believes the near-term target is achievable, but reaching the medium-term RoA goal of around 1.7% could prove challenging.

UBS has a 'Sell' rating on IndusInd Bank, with a target price of ₹870 per share. The brokerage said the bank's second-quarter profit of around ₹1,240 crore was 12% above its estimate, supported by stronger fee income and lower credit costs.
NII rose 3.6% year-on-year, but NIM declined sequentially to 3.23%, reflecting pressure from FCNR(B)-related yields and changes in the loan and deposit mix.
Other income increased 36% year-on-year, supported in part by foreign exchange income linked to FCNR(B) deposits and investment gains. Core fee income relative to assets improved to 1.35% from 1.20%.
Operating expenses rose 7% quarter-on-quarter. Pre-provision operating profit (PPoP) grew 4% on a reported basis and around 15% on a normalised basis, according to UBS.

RoA improved to 0.87% from a normalised 0.63%. Gross and net NPAs declined to around 2.7% and 0.8%, respectively. However, UBS flagged a weak current account and savings account (CASA) mix and funding cost pressures as constraints on margin recovery.

title: IndusInd Bank shares buck the trend after Q2 results; Here's how high the stock can go
